title: Stage 2: Clean and load staging
summary: Turn raw text into typed, de-duplicated rows with one INSERT ... SELECT.

steps.title: Cleaning in the SELECT
body: Cleaning happens in the **SELECT** of an `INSERT ... SELECT`. One expression per problem:
`ROUND` before the cast matters: `9.99 * 100` is `998.9999999999999` in floating point, and a bare CAST would truncate it to 998.
Duplicates: once cleaned, the twice-exported lines are identical, and the primary key rejects the second copy. `INSERT OR IGNORE` skips them instead of failing.

code: SELECT CAST(ROUND(CAST(replace('£9.99', '£', '') AS REAL) * 100) AS INTEGER),
steps.explain: Without ROUND, 998.999... is truncated to 998. One cent per line, every night, adds up.

steps.title: Preview the cleaning
prompt: Before loading, preview. Return **order_ref**, **iso_date** (the date in `YYYY-MM-DD`), **email** (trimmed, lower case) and **unit_cents** for **every** raw row, in any order.
Tables: `raw_orders(order_ref, order_date, customer_email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_price, channel)`: every column is text, exactly as exported.
solution: CAST(ROUND(CAST(replace(trim(unit_price), '£', '') AS REAL) * 100) AS INTEGER) AS unit_cents
setup: CREATE TABLE raw_orders (order_ref TEXT, order_date TEXT, customer_email TEXT, customer_name TEXT, isbn TEXT, title TEXT, qty TEXT, unit_price TEXT, channel TEXT);

steps.stateQuery: SELECT order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel FROM stg_orders ORDER BY order_ref, isbn
hints: `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO stg_orders (...) SELECT ... FROM raw_orders;`
The CHECK on channel only accepts lower case, so `lower(trim(channel))`.

steps.prompt: A future export contains `channel = 'phone'`. With the `INSERT OR IGNORE` load, what happens?
options: The row is silently skipped: OR IGNORE also ignores CHECK failures
The CHECK constraint fails and the whole load stops
The row is loaded with channel NULL
steps.explain: In SQLite, `OR IGNORE` skips rows that break UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL **and CHECK** constraints. Convenient for duplicates, dangerous for everything else: those phone orders would vanish from the dashboard without a word. A stricter load removes duplicates with `SELECT DISTINCT` (or ROW_NUMBER) and uses a plain INSERT, so a CHECK failure stops the load and someone decides what 'phone' means.

steps.title: Reconcile
prompt: Prove nothing was lost: return one row with **raw_lines** (distinct `order_ref`/`isbn` pairs in raw), **staged_lines** (rows in staging), and **staged_cents** (total of `qty * unit_cents` in staging).

Tables: `raw_orders(order_ref, order_date, customer_email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_price, channel)`: every column is text, exactly as exported. and `stg_orders(order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel)`.
solution: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_ref || '/' || isbn) FROM raw_orders) AS raw_lines,
(SELECT SUM(qty * unit_cents) FROM stg_orders) AS staged_cents;
setup: CREATE TABLE raw_orders (order_ref TEXT, order_date TEXT, customer_email TEXT, customer_name TEXT, isbn TEXT, title TEXT, qty TEXT, unit_price TEXT, channel TEXT);

CREATE TABLE stg_orders ( order_ref TEXT NOT NULL, order_date TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL, customer_name TEXT NOT NULL, isbn TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, qty INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (qty > 0), unit_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (unit_cents >= 0), channel TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (channel IN ('web', 'shop')), PRIMARY KEY (order_ref, isbn) );

INSERT OR IGNORE INTO stg_orders (order_ref, order_date, email, customer_name, isbn, title, qty, unit_cents, channel) SELECT trim(order_ref), CASE WHEN order_date LIKE '__/__/____' THEN substr(order_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(order_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(order_date, 1, 2) ELSE order_date END, lower(trim(customer_email)), trim(customer_name), trim(isbn), trim(title), CAST(trim(qty) AS INTEGER), CAST(ROUND(CAST(replace(trim(unit_price), '£', '') AS REAL) * 100) AS INTEGER), lower(trim(channel)) FROM raw_orders;
hints: Three scalar subqueries in one SELECT.
steps.explain: 13 lines in, 13 lines out. A reconciliation like this belongs in every pipeline.
